provenance.orgName: Eton, Buckinghamshire. Royal College of the Assumption of Saint Mary the Virgin.
provenance.p: Contains on the verso of the back page the ownership inscription of Walter Smyth (d. 1524), fellow of Eton from 1501 (BRUO 1720): 'Walteri Smythe Eton'. However, across the top of the verso of the first leaf (sig. a1v) is, in a different hand, 'Saltfletby, Omnium Sanctorum'. Smyth, who hailed from Saltfleetby (Lincs), had left the residue of his books to All Saints to form a lending library available for a year's lease to the learned of the district 'within the space of seven myles'. (For his testament and further discussion, see Willoughby, Collegiate Churches, 171--3, SC234.)

The fact that the book is now at Eton may offer presumptive evidence that it never left the college. However, the ex libris for All Saints at Saltfleetby is strong evidence against that assumption, and Willoughby has suggested that the book was received by, and marked for, the parish library but came to be muddled up in the books of Richard Lylly, rector of Saltfleetby from October 1547 until his death by April 1572, at least one of whose books got to Eton after his death (Bg.8.25).

The book's medieval presence at the college is to be treated with caution. The first certain evidence for Eton is the early seventeenth-century binding by the local binder, 'Vincent' Williamson (on whom see P. Morgan in The Library, 5th ser. 26 (1971), 80).
